Conjecture: Roe-cohomological concentration: HX^1(X_f) vanishes for random f, separating natural-proof properties from κ
Statement: Let f : {0,1}^n -> {0,1} be drawn uniformly at random and let (X_f, d_f) be the KW-metric space with d_f instantiated as Hamming distance on X_f = f^{-1}(0) ⊔ f^{-1}(1). For the controlled radius R = 1 and the discrete coarse coboundary operator δ on the Roe-style cochain complex C^*_{coarse}(X_f), define h^1(f) := dim_R HX^1(X_f) = dim ker(δ^1) − dim im(δ^0). The sub-conjecture (instance of axiom A3, anti-natural-proofs) asserts: (i) for n ∈ {3,4,5,6} the empirical mean of h^1(f) over uniform f tends to 0 as n grows, with Pr[h^1(f) > 0] ≤ exp(−Ω(n)); (ii) for the explicit family f_n = PARITY_n, h^1(f_n) ≥ n − 1, so the trace pairing ⟨c, T⟩ realizes κ(PARITY_n) ≥ log(R)·(n−1)/n with R = 2; (iii) consequently κ is not a 'large' property in the Razborov–Rudich sense, since it fails the largeness criterion on the uniform ensemble while remaining nonzero on explicit functions, blocking the natural-proofs obstruction to A1.
Strategy: Python/NumPy/SciPy protocol, runtime budget ≤ 90 s. (1) For each n ∈ {3,4,5,6}: enumerate X = {0,1}^n; build the Hamming graph G_R with edge set {(x,y) : d_H(x,y) ≤ R} for R=1. Build sparse δ^0 : R^X -> R^{E_bi} and δ^1 : R^{E_bi} -> R^{T_bi} (bichromatic triangles). Compute h^1 = dim ker(δ^1) − rank(δ^0) via scipy.sparse.linalg matrix_rank on small dense blocks (sizes ≤ 2^6·6 are tractable). Record the empirical histogram of h^1 and the fraction with h^1 > 0. (3) Explicit arm: same pipeline with f = PARITY_n; verify h^1(PARITY_n) ≥ n−1. (4) Compute the trace pairing ⟨c,T⟩ for the canonical PARITY cocycle c (sign of x_1⊕…⊕x_n on bichromatic edges) against the propagation-2 averaging operator T = (1/|X|)·1_{d≤2}; verify log|⟨c,T⟩| / log 2 ≥ (n−1)/n. FAIL signals revision of A3 or of the Hamming surrogate for d_f.
